doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Venuti, Billie Rogers and Henry Jerome
title: Working for Venuti and writing for him
summary: Venuti disliked running a big band; Mandel stayed six to nine months and wrote backgrounds between one-nighters.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: [Laughs] How is he to work for?

Great! He couldn’t have cared less about how the band sounded, to him, in those days to get booked, you had to have a big band, he hated big bands. He didn’t hate them, he just didn’t want to have anything to do with – he was like Louis Armstrong, he didn’t want anything to do with running one.
I guess maybe Teagarden too, well Teagarden liked having his band I think.
For a while. ‘Cause he had a good big band, he had good people and he had played in big bands a lot himself.
So, how long were you with Venuti?
Oh… somewhere, six to nine months, something like that.

Yeah, I wrote backgrounds and things, you know we were doing one nighters all the time, I didn’t have much time to write anything. Now and then we’d sit down in the theatre… and yeah, I was always fooling around with something.
